question: In scikit-learn LogisticRegression, what is the default C and does a smaller C mean stronger or weaker regularization?
answer: The default C in scikit-learn LogisticRegression is 1.0 [S1]/ [S2]. A smaller C means stronger regularization [S1].

citations.title: Ml Model Diagnostics Handbook
citations.text:
3. Regularization Strength in scikit-learn
In scikit-learn LogisticRegression the parameter C is the inverse of the regularization strength: a
smaller C means stronger regularization, and the default is C=1.0. For Ridge regression the
parameter alpha works the opposite way: a larger alpha means stronger shrinkage.
L2 regularization (ridge) shrinks all weights toward zero; L1 regularization (lasso) can set some
weights exactly to zero and therefore performs feature selection.

S3.text: Overfitting mitigation guide OVERFITTING MITIGATION GUIDE - TracePilot demo course pack (Machine Learning Fundamentals) Original educational material, CC BY 4.0, (c) Faris Mohamed Kishtah. 1. What overfitting means in practice A model overfits when its training accuracy is far higher than its validation accuracy. The gap between the two (train accuracy minus validation accuracy) is the simplest warning sign. 2. L2 regularization (weight decay) L2 regularization adds a penalty proportional to the sum of squared weights to the loss, which shrinks weights toward zero without usually making them exactly zero. Advantages: it is smooth, works with gradient-based optimizers, and keeps all features.
